state.case_summary:
A 42-year-old African American male presented with a 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and a 50-pound weight loss. He had been hospitalized 6 months prior for hypoxia. He had been treated with prednisone previously.

Patient had symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints (MCPs) and interphalangeal joints (IPs), preventing fist formation. Dorsal MCPs had ulcers, distal fingers were dyspigmented and atrophic. Capillaroscopy was normal, and palmar IP creases had ulcerated lichenoid papules. Oxford Scale muscle strength was 5 of 5 throughout. Auscultation revealed bibasilar rales.

- Laboratory Tests:    - Aldolase: 4.5 U/L (normal)    - Creatine kinase: 32 U/L (depressed)    - Ferritin: 1543 ng/mL (elevated)    - T lymphocyte counts: CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL (lymphocytopenia)    - Positive for anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies    - Positive for immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies (19.5 units)    - Negative results: HIV, anti–Scl-70 antibodies, anti–β2-glycoprotein 1 antibodies, lupus anticoagulant, cryoglobulins, anti–Mi-2 antibodies    - Normal: prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, tissue thromboplastin- Imaging Studies:    - Initial Chest CT showed hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities    - Follow-up Chest CT revealed worsening interstitial lung disease    - Other Tests:    - Bronchoscopy revealed plaquelike lesions    - Transbronchial nodal aspiration of mediastinal nodes was negative for carcinomas/granulomas    - Pulmonary function tests showed restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted)    - Skin biopsy showed orthokeratosis with rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction, minimal basal vacuolar change, pigment incontinence, and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi in deep dermal vessels

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Systemic lupus erythematosus
B. Antiphospholipid syndrome
C. Dermatomyositis
D. Antimelanoma differentiation associated gene 5 clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis
